Complainant versus A1) Sh. Rajender Kumar S/o Sh. Laxmi Narain M/s Khandelwal Store, C-7, Sunny Bazar Road, Uttam Nagar, New Delhi-59 R/o B-3, J.J. Colony, Hastsal, Uttam Nagar, New Delhi - 59. A2) M/s Karnal Milk Foods Ltd., 134 Km Stone, G.T. Road, Dadupur, Kamal (Haryana) A3) Sh. Pramod Kumar S/o Sh. C.J. Singh M/s Karnal Milk Foods Ltd., 134 Km Stone, G.T. Road, Dadupur, Kamal (Haryana) R/o Village Bhagwanpur, Distt. Haridwar (Uttaranchal) ... Accused person. (Since proclaimed offender vide order dated 22.11.2016) Cc No. 41513/2016 Page No. 1/10 Da vs Rajender Kumar etc. Judgment: Da vs Rajender Kumar Etc. on 5 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106688188/ 1 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 195
texts.facts: Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106688188/ 1 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 195 4 (herein after referred to as PFA Act), alleging that the accused persons have violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules. 2. As per the complaint, on 28.01.2005, the Food Inspector (herein after referred to as FI) Shri V.P.S. Chaudhary and Field Assistant (herein after referred as FA) Shri Balwant Shah under the supervision of Local Health Authority (herein after referred to as LHA)/SDM) Shri Mohd Ali Ashraf visited the premises of M/s Khandelwal Store, C-7, Sunny Bazar Road, Uttam Nagar, New Delhi-59, where accused No. 1 Rajender Kumar was found conducting the business of food articles stored there, including "Ghee" for sale for human consumption, bearing identical label declaration. The sample consisted of 3x500 ml sealed plastic jar of 'Ghee' having identical label declaration. The sample was taken under the supervision / direction of Sh. M.A. Ashraf, SDM/LHA. The sample of "Ghee" was taken as such in original sealed condition. The Food Inspector divided the sample then and there into three equal parts. Each sample counter part containing the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules. The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample counter parts. Notice in Form VI was given to accused No.1 Rajender Kumar and the price of sample was also given to him vide vendor receipt DA vs Rajender Kumar etc. dated 28-01-2005. Panchnama too was prepared at the spot. All the documents prepared by F.I. were signed by accused No.1 Rajender Kumar and the other witness Sh. Balwant Shah, FA. Before starting sample proceeding efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward, as such Sh. Balwant Shah, FA was joined as witness. 3. One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA code No. 91/LHA/11058 was also sent to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact condition and remaining two counter-parts were deposited with the LHA in intact condition. Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the same non-conforming to the standards prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules. The report of the Public Analyst is as follows: "The sample does not conform to standard because Reichert value is less than the prescribed minimum limit of 28 and BR exceed the prescribed maximum limit of 43." 4. It is the case of the complainant that accused No. 1 Rajender Kumar was the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s Khandelwal Store, C-7, Sunny Bazar Road, Uttam Nagar, New Delhi- 59 at the time of sampling and he is incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the shop. The vendor has purchased the sampled commodity from accused No. 2 M/s Karnal Milk Foods Ltd., 134 KM Stone, G.T. Road, Dadupur, Kamal (Haryana). Accused No. 2 M/s Karnal Milk Foods Ltd. has nominated accused No. 3 Pramod Kumar as its nominee under PFA Act and as such he was in-charge and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the DA vs Rajender Kumar etc. company along with Ms Karnal Milk Foods Ltd. 5. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 30.06.2005 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(a)(m) of PFA Act, 1954 as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act against the accused persons. Da vs Rajender Kumar Etc. on 5 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106688188/ 2 6. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 30.06.2005. The accused thereafter exercised their option of analysing the counter part through CFL under section 13 (2) of the PFA Act. Based on the report of the CFL as well as evidence led in pre charge evidence, charge was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) (a) PFA Act being violation of Section 2(ia)(a)&(m) of PFA Act, 1954 to which accused person pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. During the trial accused No. 3 Pramod Kumar was declared proclaimed offender vide order dated 22.11.2016. 7. At the trial, the prosecution examined three witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 FI V.P.S. Chaudhary, PW-2 SDM/LHA Sh M.A. Ashraf and PW-3 FA Sh Balwant Shah. PW-1 and PW-3 were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh M.A. Ashraf. These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their DA vs Rajender Kumar etc. identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the three plastic jars of of Ghee sealed 500 ml each, bearing identical label declaration, dividing the sample commodity into three equal parts by putting one originally sealed plastic jar of Ghee as one counterpart, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex. PW- 1/A, Notice in Form VI Ex.PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex.PW-1/C. Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample alongwith a copy of Memo in Form VII in a sealed packet and another copy of Memo in Form VII in another sealed cover were sent separately to PA vide receipt Ex.PW1/D on 31.01.2005 and remaining two counterparts alongwith two copies of Memo in Form VII in a sealed packet were deposited with LHA vide LHA Receipt Ex. PW 1/E. Thereafter PA Report Ex.PW1/F was received and PW-1 FI V.P.S. Chaudhary further investigated the case and sent letter Ex.PW1/G to STO Ward No. 61 to disclose the constitution of M/s Khandelwal store and received its report stating that no such firm was found registered with Sales Tax. PW-1 FI V.P.S. Chaudhary also sent letter Ex.PW1/H to vendor and received its reply Ex.PW1/H1 and documents Mark X stating that he had purchased the sample commodity from M/s Karnal Milk Food Ltd. 134, K.M Stone GT Road Karnal. PW-1 also sent letter to M/s Karnal Milk Food Ltd and received its reply Ex.PW1/J and documents Mark Y & Y1. Thereafter after completion of investigation the entire case file was put before the concerned SDM/LHA who forwarded the same to the then Director of PFA for obtaining the sanction and DA vs Rajender Kumar etc. the then Director PFA granted his consent for prosecution against the accused persons vide Ex.PW1/L. Thereafter, the present complaint Ex.PW-1/M was filed in the Court. Then intimation letter Ex.PW1/N alongwith copy of PA Reports were sent to accused persons through post vide postal receipt Ex.PW1/O. The witnesses were duly cross examined by the Ld Defence Counsel. 8. Statement of the accused under section 313 Cr.PC were recorded on 24.05.2017 wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Thereafter the matter was listed for defence evidence. 9. In their defence evidence, the accused examined one Dr. O.P. Singhal. Thereafter vide order dated 20.11.2017 defence evidence was closed and the matter was listed for final arguments. texts.arguments: On this basis, the defence is seeking to claim that the samples were not representative due to said 'variations of more than 0.3%' in PA and CFL report. 15.In this regard, the defence strongly relies upon the judgement titled as Kanshi Nath v. State [2005(2) FAC 219], informing DA vs Rajender Kumar etc. that the said ruling has been constantly followed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in many subsequent cases. 16.This issue of variation was considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Delhi Administration vs Vidya Gupta Criminal Appeal No. 625 of 2018 dated 24.04.2018 wherein it was held that the finding of Hon'ble High Court in Kanshi Nath vs State and State vs Mahender Kumar & Ors, which hold that if in the comparison of reports of PA and the Director vast variations are found, then the samples are not representative, is improper.
